title: CRITICAL: the gateway-token kill switch does not stop a running agent
description:
Found while stopping the \$49.80 runaway (run_f15efdfb...). D17 states that revoking a run gateway token is the kill switch that works even on a wedged or adversarial agent. It does not work.

What was tried, in order, and what happened:
  1. POST /api/runs/<id>/stop        -> state became "stopping"; model calls CONTINUED (by design, a clean stop finishes in-flight work — but see below).
  2. Revoked the run gateway token in D1 (run_gateway_token.revoked_at set, 1 row written) -> model calls CONTINUED for several more minutes.
  3. wrangler containers delete <app> -> calls STOPPED within ~2 minutes.
Only destroying the container actually halted the spend. That is a sledgehammer: it removes the application for every run and needs a redeploy to restore.

TWO DEFECTS HERE:
a) The revocation is not enforced on the request path. Either the gateway proxy does not check revoked_at per request, or it caches the token. Whatever the cause, the credential-layer kill switch the design relies on is decorative. Fix it so a revoked token is refused on the very next request, and add a test that revokes mid-run and asserts the next call is rejected.
b) A CLEAN STOP HAS NO TEETH WHEN THE BUDGET IS ALREADY BREACHED. Finishing in-flight work is right for an ordinary stop and wrong for a runaway — this run was at 2x its budget with no durable output for over four hours, and the clean stop kept it spending. There needs to be a hard stop for the budget case: revoke first, then let the clean stop unwind. tk cloud stop should probably grow --now (or the budget trip should take that path automatically), so the operator is not left choosing between a stop that does not stop and deleting infrastructure.

Note this compounds cts: the budget could not trip because of the pagination bug, AND once a human noticed, the intended remedy did not work either. Two independent failures of the same safety property — the first let it start, the second stopped it being stoppable.

acceptance_criteria: A revoked run gateway token is refused on the next request, proven by a test that revokes mid-run; a budget-exhausted or operator-forced stop halts model traffic without deleting the container application; tk cloud stop offers a hard variant and says which it performed.
